# tuiksdmx

**An authenticated, metadata-driven R client for the TÜİK (Turkish
Statistical Institute) SDMX REST API.**

Discover dataflows · Understand structures · Build validated queries ·
Retrieve statistical data

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pkgdown-AB2328.svg)](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-AB2328.svg)](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/LICENSE.md)

> **Development release (`0.0.0.9000`).** `tuiksdmx` is currently
> distributed through GitHub, not CRAN. TÜİK SDMX endpoints require
> authentication. Dataflow structures and service behaviour may change;
> examples below use a Dataflow verified during development.

## Why tuiksdmx?

SDMX datasets are multidimensional. To construct a meaningful query, you
may need to know the Dataflow, its data structure definition (DSD),
dimension order, codes and time range. **`tuiksdmx` uses this metadata
to make the process easier and more reproducible**, without requiring
you to manually assemble an SDMX key for ordinary workflows.

| Discover | Understand | Query | Retrieve |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Search Dataflows and inspect their metadata | Explore DSD dimensions, concepts, codelists and labels | Validate filters and construct structure-aware keys | Download observations and optionally decode labels |

The package also offers **observed availability**: inspect which
dimension codes occur in data for a specified request, rather than
assuming every code in a codelist has observations.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub using **pak** (recommended):

``` r

install.packages("pak")  # Run once, if not already installed
pak::pak("MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx")
```

Alternatively, use **remotes**, a familiar option for installing R
packages from GitHub:

``` r

install.packages("remotes")  # Run once, if not already installed
remotes::install_github("MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx")
```

Both methods install the GitHub development version; the package is not
yet on CRAN. Then load it:

``` r

library(tuiksdmx)
```

For contributors working from a local source checkout,
`devtools::load_all()` is also available.

## Quick start

### 1. Configure authentication

TÜİK SDMX requests require an API key. For everyday use, store it in
your personal `.Renviron` file (open it with `usethis::edit_r_environ()`
if needed):

``` text
TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY=YOUR_OWN_API_KEY
```

Restart R after saving. The package will read this environment variable
automatically. **Never commit credentials** or paste access tokens into
issues, scripts or notebooks.

You can also supply an API key explicitly through `api_key` or set
`TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY` for the current session; see [Authentication
options](#authentication).

### 2. Discover Dataflows

You do **not** need to know a Dataflow ID in advance. Browse the
authenticated catalogue or search by subject:

``` r

# Retrieve the catalogue of Dataflows
flows <- tuik_dataflows()

# View identifiers and their Turkish / English names
head(flows[c("dataflow_id", "name_tr", "name_en")], 10)

# Search the catalogue in Turkish (accent-insensitive matching)
tuik_search_dataflows("tüketici fiyat", limit = 10)

# Or search by English terminology
tuik_search_dataflows("consumer price", language = "en", limit = 10)
```

Choose a `dataflow_id` from the results. The remainder of this example
uses the CPI Dataflow `DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01`, which was inspected during
package development; live catalogues can change.

### 3. Explore a Dataflow

``` r

# Inspect dimensions and metadata without retrieving observations
tuik_explore("DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01")

# List codes and their descriptions for a dimension
tuik_explore("DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01", dimension = "DEGISIM")

# Search descriptions in another dimension
tuik_explore(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  dimension = "COICOP_2018",
  search = "gıda"
)
```

### 4. Retrieve observations

If you know the Dataflow ID and time window, you can make a request
directly:

``` r

cpi <- tuik_get_data(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period   = "2026-01"
)

head(cpi)
```

This requests **all series for the specified observation period**. It is
not limited to a single CPI indicator.

### 5. Narrow the result with structured filters

``` r

chosen <- list(
  REF_AREA = "TR",
  FREQ = "M",
  DEGISIM = "1",
  SINIFLAMA_DUZEYI = "2"
)

# Check the filters against the structure
tuik_explore("DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01", filters = chosen)

cpi_selected <- tuik_get_data(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  filters = chosen,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  allow_all = TRUE,
  labels = "tr"
)
```

> **Caution — partial filters can trigger broad downloads.** With a
> partial series key, `allow_all = TRUE` explicitly permits retrieval of
> all series within the requested period, followed by **local filtering
> in R**. It is **not** a download-size, memory or time limit. The
> partial/wildcard key patterns tested during development were not
> accepted by the TÜİK service. For targeted server-side requests,
> specify a complete set of series key dimensions.

**Time dimension detail:** `TIME_PERIOD` refers to observation time and
is controlled with `start_period` / `end_period`, not placed in the
series-key `filters`. `YAYIM_DONEMI` is a separate DSD series dimension.

### 6. Target one observed CPI series (verified example)

A complete DSD key avoids the broad download used by partial-filter
queries. The following combination was confirmed against the live TÜİK
SDMX service on **23 October 2026** for the **January 2026 general CPI
index (2025 reference year)**:

``` r

cpi_profile <- tuik_flow_profile("DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01")

cpi_filters <- list(
  REF_AREA = "TR",
  FREQ = "M",
  SINIFLAMA_DUZEYI = "TUFE",
  DEGISIM = "1",
  OZEL_KAPSAM_TUFE = "_Z",
  BASE_PER = "2025",
  YAYIM_DONEMI = "2026_01",
  COICOP_1999 = "_Z",
  COICOP_2018 = "0",
  INDICATOR = "F_TFE"
)

# Check that all codes belong to their codelists
validation <- tuik_validate_filters(cpi_profile, filters = cpi_filters)

# A full key is sent to the API; allow_all is not needed
cpi_one <- tuik_get_data(
  cpi_profile,
  filters = cpi_filters,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01"
)

cpi_one[c("TIME_PERIOD", "OBS_VALUE")]
```

The tested request returned **one observation**, `2026-01` with
`OBS_VALUE = 116` (about 2.52 seconds in that run). This is a **specific
publication vintage** (`YAYIM_DONEMI = "2026_01"`), not an instruction
to always select the latest release. Future values or Dataflow
structures may change.

**Valid codes do not guarantee an observed series.**
[`tuik_validate_filters()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_validate_filters.md)
checks codelist membership, **not** whether all selected codes occur
together. For example, `OZEL_KAPSAM_TUFE = "GT_1"` and
`COICOP_1999 = "0"` were individually valid codes, but that combination
returned HTTP 404 during the test. The actually observed series used
`_Z` for both dimensions. Inspect bounded observations or use
[`tuik_available_codes()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_available_codes.md)
to explore observed values before composing a full key. Observed codes
in isolation still do not guarantee every cross-dimensional combination.

## Metadata, profiles and observed availability

Use a profile when inspecting or querying the same Dataflow repeatedly:

``` r

profile <- tuik_flow_profile("DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01")

# Series-key dimensions and their associated codelists
tuik_filter_dimensions(profile)

# Theoretical domain defined by a codelist
tuik_dimension_codes(profile, dimension = "DEGISIM")

# Codes actually present in the returned observations for this request
observed <- tuik_available_codes(
  profile,
  dimension = "COICOP_2018",
  filters = list(
    REF_AREA = "TR",
    FREQ = "M",
    SINIFLAMA_DUZEYI = "2",
    DEGISIM = "1"
  ),
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  allow_all = TRUE
)

observed
```

**Codelist domain ≠ observed availability.** A codelist describes
permissible codes;
[`tuik_available_codes()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_available_codes.md)
derives observed codes from retrieved observations for the specified
request. It does **not** implement SDMX ContentConstraint queries.

## Authentication

The package supports three ways to provide an API key:

| Method | Example | When to use it |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Environment variable (recommended)** | Set `TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY` in your personal `.Renviron` | Regular, reproducible use without keys in scripts |
| **Explicit argument** | `tuik_get_data(id, ..., api_key = api)` | When a key is supplied securely by your application |
| **Current-session environment** | `Sys.setenv(TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY = api)` | Temporary sessions; does not edit `.Renviron` |

An explicit `api_key` takes precedence over the environment variable. It
is also supported by authenticated discovery, exploration, profiles and
metadata operations. The object named `api` above is a placeholder for a
key obtained securely; do not store it in tracked scripts or print
credentials or tokens.

## Download safeguards and performance

| Request | Behaviour |
|:---|:---|
| A Dataflow ID with a bounded time range and no series filters | Downloads all series within that period |
| Complete DSD series-key filters | Builds a targeted server-side SDMX key |
| Partial series-key filters | Requires deliberate `allow_all = TRUE`, with potentially broad retrieval and subsequent local filtering |
| Unbounded request involving all/partial series | Additionally requires `allow_unbounded = TRUE` |
| Repeated requests against one Dataflow | Reuse [`tuik_flow_profile()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_flow_profile.md) to avoid repeated structure discovery where possible |

Response times can vary considerably. Selected development requests took
approximately one second on some attempts and over a minute on others;
the cause was not confirmed. A short period or `allow_all = TRUE` does
not guarantee a small response.

## Guides

The README is a starting point, not a complete function reference. Six
guides are included in the package and available on the [documentation
website](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/):

| Guide | What it covers |
|:---|:---|
| [Getting started](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/getting-started.html) | Discovery, exploration, periods, filtering and retrieval |
| [Metadata and DSD](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/metadata-and-dsd.html) | Dataflows, dimensions, DSDs, concepts and codelists |
| [Filtering and performance](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/filtering-and-performance.html) | Full vs partial keys, safeguards and request performance |
| [Observed availability](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/observed-availability.html) | Codelist domains versus observed codes |
| [Authentication and secure use](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/authentication.html) | API key options, tokens and reproducible credential handling |
| [Labels and decoding](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/labels-and-decoding.html) | Turkish/English labels, dimension selection and decoding data already retrieved |

After installation, use `browseVignettes("tuiksdmx")` to view built
guides in R. For individual function arguments and examples, open R help
pages such as
[`?tuik_get_data`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_data.md),
[`?tuik_search_dataflows`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_search_dataflows.md),
and
[`?tuik_decode_data`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_decode_data.md).

**Labels and readable outputs:** `tuik_get_data(..., labels = "tr")` can
add Turkish code descriptions; `labels = "en"` or `"both"` are also
supported. The `label_dimensions` argument controls which dimensions are
decoded. See the [Labels and decoding
guide](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/articles/labels-and-decoding.html)
for a worked example.

The [pkgdown documentation
website](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/) brings together the
[function reference](https://mfatihtuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/),
all six guides and the changelog.

## Scope and limitations

`tuiksdmx` is a **focused SDMX client**. It is not intended to duplicate
broader TÜİK portal resource discovery, Excel downloads or geographic
functionality provided by other tooling such as `tuikr`.

The package does **not** claim support for server-side partial/wildcard
SDMX keys, ContentConstraint querying, streaming, or guaranteed hard
limits on downloads. Selected CPI and birth Dataflows were used during
development; success with these does not establish compatibility with
every Dataflow or future service configuration.

## Development and quality

The project has a `testthat` suite and an automated [R CMD check
workflow](https://github.com/MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
for Ubuntu, Windows and macOS. The latest local development validation
reported **534 passing expectations**, **0 errors**, **0 warnings** and
**1 note** (the local environment could not verify its current time).
The subsequent three-platform CI run completed successfully; results are
checks of this development snapshot, not a guarantee of live API
availability.

Contributions and reproducible bug reports can be shared through [GitHub
Issues](https://github.com/MFatihTuzen/tuiksdmx/issues). **Do not attach
credentials, tokens or private session files.**

# Package index

## Find statistical datasets

Discover and search SDMX Dataflows.

- [`tuik_dataflows()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_dataflows.md)
  : List TÜİK SDMX Dataflows
- [`tuik_search_dataflows()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_search_dataflows.md)
  : Search TÜİK SDMX Dataflows
- [`tuik_get_dataflow()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_dataflow.md)
  : Retrieve a single TÜİK SDMX Dataflow
- [`tuik_explore()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_explore.md)
  : Explore a TUIK SDMX Dataflow before downloading observations

## Inspect metadata and dimensions

Explore Data Structures, code lists, concepts and dimensions.

- [`tuik_flow_profile()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_flow_profile.md)
  : Build a profile for a TÜİK SDMX Dataflow
- [`tuik_get_dsd()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_dsd.md)
  : Retrieve a TÜİK SDMX Data Structure Definition
- [`tuik_dimensions()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_dimensions.md)
  : Extract dimensions from a TÜİK SDMX DSD
- [`tuik_key_dimensions()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_key_dimensions.md)
  : Return the dimensions used in an SDMX series key
- [`tuik_attributes()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_attributes.md)
  : Extract attributes from a TÜİK SDMX DSD
- [`tuik_measures()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_measures.md)
  : Extract measures from a TÜİK SDMX DSD
- [`tuik_get_codelist()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_codelist.md)
  : Retrieve a TÜİK SDMX Codelist
- [`tuik_dimension_codes()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_dimension_codes.md)
  : Retrieve codes for a DSD dimension
- [`tuik_get_concept_scheme()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_concept_scheme.md)
  : Retrieve a TÜİK SDMX ConceptScheme
- [`tuik_concepts()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_concepts.md)
  : Retrieve concepts used by a TÜİK Dataflow
- [`tuik_search_concepts()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_search_concepts.md)
  : Search concepts used by a TÜİK Dataflow

## Build and validate queries

Use structured dimension filters and validated SDMX keys.

- [`tuik_filter_template()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_filter_template.md)
  : Create a filter template for a TÜİK SDMX Dataflow
- [`tuik_filter_dimensions()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_filter_dimensions.md)
  : Show required filters for a TÜİK SDMX Dataflow
- [`tuik_missing_filters()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_missing_filters.md)
  : Identify missing SDMX key filters
- [`tuik_validate_filters()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_validate_filters.md)
  : Validate SDMX filter values against referenced Codelists
- [`tuik_build_key()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_build_key.md)
  : Build an SDMX data key

## Retrieve and interpret observations

Download observations, interpret labels and inspect observed
availability.

- [`tuik_get_data()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_get_data.md)
  : Retrieve data from a TÜİK SDMX Dataflow
- [`tuik_decode_data()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_decode_data.md)
  : Add SDMX code labels to an observation table
- [`tuik_available_codes()`](https://MFatihTuzen.github.io/tuiksdmx/reference/tuik_available_codes.md)
  : Retrieve codes observed in a Dataflow for a time window
